title: Towards Benchmarking Transformer Models for Biomedical Text Simplification
abstract: Biomedical texts typically contain a high level of technical terminology and complex sentence structures, which limits their comprehensibility for readers without domain expertise. Text simplification, a natural language processing problem, aims to transform complex texts into a more readable and accessible form while preserving their original semantic content. Especially in biomedical texts, simplification can play an essential role in making scientific information understandable to patients and the general public. In this context, this study investigates the text simplification performance of pre-trained general-purpose and domain-specific language models (PLMs) for biomedical texts. The experiments utilize the Cochrane-Simplification dataset, which comprises technical abstracts from systematic reviews and their corresponding plain language summaries. General-purpose models and summarization tuned variants (BART-Large, BART-Large-CNN, BART-Large-XSum, PEGASUS-Large, PEGASUS-XSum, T5 and FLAN-T5) are compared alongside domain-specific models (BioBARTv2-Large, SciFive, Clinical-T5) under comparable fine-tuning settings. The models were compared using ROUGE, BLEU, BERTScore and SARI metrics to measure textual similarity and semantic coherence. The results indicate that BART based models achieve superior performance in the medical text simplification task.

title: Delta Sets as Formal Boundary Objects in Incomplete Theories
abstract: This paper introduces Delta sets ($\Delta$) as formally defined regions of non-derivability within a formal theory, establishing a precise link between logical incompleteness and the boundary-based formulations of the TNA framework. We prove that for any incomplete theory, the Delta set is non-empty and constitutes the structural boundary of the system ($\partial\Omega_T = \Delta$). The study demonstrates that these sets induce a partition of the domain and correspond to regions of zero derivability reliability ($R=0$). Furthermore, we provide a formal construction of boundary pressure ($F_B$) derived from the magnitude and weighting of the Delta set, showing that incompleteness fundamentally generates a structural pressure for theoretical extension. This results in a formal grounding for the transition from axiomatic systems to dynamic boundary structures

title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence into Financial Investment Decision-making: Opportunities and Constraints
abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into financial investment decision-making has emerged as a transformative development in modern financial markets. AI- driven technologies, including machine learning algorithms, predictive analytics and automated trading systems, enable investors and financial institutions to process vast volumes of data, identify complex patterns, and enhance the precision and speed of investment decisions. This paper examines the opportunities offered by AI integration in investment decision-making, such as improved portfolio optimization, enhanced risk management, reduction of cognitive and behavioral biases and increased market efficiency. Simultaneously, the study critically analyses the constraints associated with AI adaptation, including data quality issues, model interpretability, algorithmic bias, ethical concerns, regulatory challenges, and the risk of excessive dependence on automated systems. Drawing on an extensive review of existing literature and industry practices, the paper highlights the need for a balanced human-AI collaborative approach to investment decision-making. The study concludes that while AI significantly strengthens analytical capabilities and decision efficiency, its effective integration requires robust governance frameworks, transparency, and human oversight to ensure sustainable and responsible investment practices.

title: Decoding-Enhanced Bidirectional Encoder Representations with Attention-Based Pooling Mechanism for Insurance Fraud Detections
abstract: Insurance fraud is an ongoing threat to the financial sustainability of insurance providers, resulting in substantial economic losses and enhanced operational expenses. Conventional rule-based and classical machine learning approaches often struggle to capture the semantic complexity, long-range dependencies, and contextual nuances inherent in large-scale insurance claim data. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Decoding-Enhanced Bidirectional Encoder Representations with Attention-Based Pooling (DE-BERT-AP) framework for accurate and robust insurance fraud detection. The proposed technique leverages bidirectional contextual embeddings to capture deep semantic relationships within claim descriptions and connected textual records. A decoding-enhanced representation learning module is incorporated to refine latent feature representations by reconstructing and reinforcing discriminative patterns relevant to fraudulent behavior. An attention-based pooling mechanism also adaptively prioritizes informative tokens and claim segments, allowing the model to focus on important signs of fraud while ignoring noise that isn't relevant. The integrated design efficiently captures both local and global contextual dependencies, thereby developing classification robustness across a wide range of fraud scenarios. Many experiments performed on real-world and benchmark insurance claim datasets recognized that the proposed DE-BERT-AP framework surpasses present deep learning and transformer-based baselines in accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-scores, while preserving computational efficiency. Overall, the results highlight the efficiency of decoding-enhanced contextual learning combined with attention-driven aggregation for next-generation systems that detect intelligent insurance fraud.

title: Dynamic-SQL: an adaptive NL2SQL framework with multi-path fusion reasoning and execution feedback correction
abstract: Current NL2SQL systems degrade sharply when confronted with practical constraints such as limited prompt length and the inability to fine-tune large language models (LLMs). Performance drop is especially pronounced in complex databases, where inaccurate schema linking, vague value conditions, and weak self-correction dominate the error surface. We propose Dynamic-SQL, an adaptive framework that couples multi-path chain-of-thought fusion with execution-based feedback correction. A dense-sparse hybrid vector space is first constructed to dynamically retrieve relevant schema elements, and an LLM is leveraged to generate an explicit schema subgraph. Real-value and few-shot exemplars are then injected to enrich the prompt and sharpen value conditioning. Multiple candidate SQL statements are produced via diverse reasoning paths; their chains of thought are fused to cover latent semantic interpretations, and execution feedback is exploited for iterative self-correction until convergence. On the BIRD benchmark, Dynamic-SQL, powered by the open source qwen2.5-coder-32b-instruct, reduces the average prompt length by 50.83%, raises strict schema-linking recall from 72.63% to 90.66%, and achieves 63.23% execution accuracy. By systematically addressing schema linking, exemplar augmentation, multi-path fusion reasoning, and self-correction, the framework offers a transferable paradigm for deploying LLMs in complex database querying scenarios.

title: Unsupervised Anomaly Detection in Process-Complex Industrial Time Series: A Real-World Case Study
abstract: Industrial time-series data from real production environments exhibits substantially higher complexity than commonly used benchmark datasets, primarily due to heterogeneous, multi-stage operational processes. As a result, anomaly detection methods validated under simplified conditions often fail to generalize to industrial settings. This work presents an empirical study on a unique dataset collected from fully operational industrial machinery, explicitly capturing pronounced process-induced variability. We evaluate which model classes are capable of capturing this complexity, starting with a classical Isolation Forest baseline and extending to multiple autoencoder architectures. Experimental results show that Isolation Forest is insufficient for modeling the non-periodic, multi-scale dynamics present in the data, whereas autoencoders consistently perform better. Among them, temporal convolutional autoencoders achieve the most robust performance, while recurrent and variational variants require more careful tuning.

title: TableMaster: A Recipe to Advance Table Understanding with Language Models
abstract: Tables serve as a fundamental format for representing structured relational data. While current language models (LMs) excel at many text-based tasks, they still face challenges in table understanding due to the complex characteristics of tabular data, such as their structured nature. In this paper, we aim to enhance LMs for improved table understanding. We identify four key challenges: 1) difficulty in locating target data, 2) deficiency in table semantics, 3) numerical inaccuracies in textual reasoning, and 4) semantic inflexibility in symbolic reasoning. To address these issues, we propose TableMaster, a recipe and comprehensive framework that integrates multiple solutions to overcome these obstacles. TableMaster first extracts relevant table content and verbalizes it with enriched semantic context. Additionally, we introduce adaptive reasoning, a flexible approach that dynamically adjusts between textual and symbolic reasoning, tailoring the reasoning process to each query. Extensive analyses and experiments demonstrate our findings and the effectiveness of TableMaster. On the WikiTQ dataset, TableMaster achieves an accuracy of 78.13% using GPT-4o-mini, surpassing existing baselines. We hope this work will serve as a practical step toward more robust and reliable table understanding.

title: ПРАВОВІ РИЗИКИ ВИКОРИСТАННЯ ШІ ТА ІНТЕЛЕКТУАЛЬНОГО КАПІТАЛУ В УПРАВЛІННІ ПІДПРИЄМСТВОМ ТА ЇХ НАСЛІДКИ ДЛЯ ФІНАНСОВОЇ БЕЗПЕКИ БІЗНЕСУ ТА РИНКУ ПРАЦІ
abstract: The use of artificial intelligence in the management of enterprises and in most business processes creates not only opportunities for saving resources - time, human, and financial, but also creates a source of threats. Among the objective reasons that mark the evolution of economic relations and characterize general economic progress, which cannot be stopped and should not be stopped, there are also subjective reasons for the negative impact of artificial intelligence on the system of labour relations, financial security of business, the state of the labour market, which can be eliminated through the mechanisms of legal regulation of the sphere of use of artificial intelligence in business processes and socio-economic systems. The legal risks of using artificial intelligence in the management of enterprises and the legal risks of using intellectual capital in the activities of enterprises are specified, such as infringement of intellectual property rights, unsettled rights to the results of intellectual activity of enterprise employees, leakage of trade secrets and know-how, conflicts regarding property rights between the employer and employee, insufficient protection of the intellectual assets of the enterprise, illegal use of intellectual resources, lack of mechanisms for reliable assessment of the value of intellectual capital, risks of loss of intellectual capital and personnel potential due to personnel turnover. The impact of legal risks of using artificial intelligence and intellectual capital on the financial security of enterprises is summarized and the possible consequences of the scaling of artificial intelligence in business processes for the state and development trends of the national labour market and its main participants are clarified. It was concluded that at the national level, the scaling of the application of artificial intelligence creates noticeable trends in the labour market, in particular, regarding the demand for digital skills from potential employees on the part of employers, a decrease in the supply of low-skilled labour, the disappearance of a number of professions and positions, and an increase in unemployment among IT specialists.

title: What the Hype? Eine Einführung in die Grundlagen des maschinellen Lernens für Kulturerbeinstitutionen (2026)
abstract: Präsentation zu Teil I + III des Workshops. Teil II und IV (Formelshow, pragmatisches Fazit) werden in Kombination mit I + III als eLecture aufbereitet. Maschinelles Lernen (ML) oder auch „Künstliche Intelligenz“ (KI) ist weiterhin das große Thema in fast allen Bereichen des menschlichen Arbeitens. Aber was offerieren diese Werkzeuge abseits des großen Hypes von „schneller, größer, besser, einfacher und schöner“ und dem damit prognostizierten Durchdringen aller Lebensbereiche? Diese digiS-Einführung hat zum Ziel, Nicht-Expert:innen im maschinellen Lernen das nötige Hintergrundwissen zu vermitteln, um sich in diesem Diskurs zurechtzufinden und Hype von sinnvoller Anwendung unterscheiden zu können. Dabei wurden u.A. folgende Fragen diskutiert: Was sind Methoden Maschinellen Lernens und wie funktionieren große (und kleine) ML-Modelle? Ist die Idee einer Intelligenz, die die menschliche mindestens nachahmt oder gar übersteigt neu? (Spoiler: nein.) Was sind LLMs, VLMs, Reasoning Architekturen oder multimodale Modelle? Was bedeuten Tokens, Embeddings, Transformer und Prompten? Und warum sind Kulturerbeeinrichtungen potentiell so wichtig für die Weiterentwicklung und/oder Regulierung von „KI“? Diese Fragen stellen sich auch, wenn es um Einordnung und Beherrschbarkeit der Werkzeuge, sowie Autonomie und Emanzipation von großen Anbietern geht. Xenia Kitaeva und Marco Klindt versuchen, ein wenig Hilfestellung beim (frei nach Kant) „(…) Ausgang der Menschen aus einer nicht ganz selbstverschuldeten Unmündigkeit“ zu bieten.

title: Graph Neural Networks with E-Commerce Security Through Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm
abstract: The rapid development of e-commerce platforms has improved the demand for robust, scalable, and intelligent security mechanisms to protect digital transactions against fraud, manipulation, and unauthorized access. Traditional security frameworks primarily rely on cryptographic primitives for authentication and data integrity but lack the ability to model the complex relational patterns inherent in e-commerce ecosystems, such as interactions among users, merchants, transactions, and devices. To address this limitation, this work proposes an integrated Graph Neural Network (GNN)-driven e-commerce security framework enhanced with the Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (ECDSA). In the proposed approach, e-commerce entities and their interactions are modeled as a dynamic graph, where GNNs learn high-level relational representations to detect anomalous behaviors, fraudulent transaction patterns, and coordinated attacks. Concurrently, ECDSA is employed to ensure strong authentication, message integrity, and non-repudiation of transactional data with minimal computational overhead, making it suitable for large-scale and real-time e-commerce environments. The synergy between GNN-based relational intelligence and elliptic curve-based cryptographic security enables both proactive threat detection and cryptographically secure transaction validation. Experimental evaluations conducted on benchmark e-commerce transaction datasets establish that the suggested system outperforms conventional machine learning methods and separate cryptographic techniques in terms of fraud detection accuracy, false positive rates, and overall transaction trustworthiness. This framework offers a promising direction for next-generation intelligent and secure e-commerce systems.

title: Quinex: Quantitative information extraction from text using open and lightweight LLMs
abstract: Extracting quantitative data from the growing body of scientific literature is a challenge central to modern research across disciplines. While recent advances in large language models have significantly facilitated automation of this traditionally time-consuming task, their computational demands limit scalability and accessibility. Smaller specialized systems offer reduced computational requirements but sacrifice accuracy, domain generalization, or the extraction of contextual details. To address these gaps, we present Quinex, a domain-agnostic framework for quantitative information extraction based on comparably small language models. Quinex identifies quantities and their associated entities, properties, and qualifiers using a multi-turn question-answering approach. By addressing the data bottleneck, considering implicit properties, and optimizing extraction order and question templates, Quinex achieves state-of-the-art F1 scores of over 98% for quantities, 82% for entities, and 87% for properties across diverse scientific genres. It goes beyond identification by normalizing units, aligning them with a unit ontology, and detailing critical qualifiers such as references, spatiotemporal scopes, and determination methods. By reducing the effort required to extract structured quantitative data from texts, Quinex enables transformative applications, including automated literature reviews, quantitative search, and trend monitoring, and sets a new benchmark for scalable, accurate, and domain-agnostic quantitative information extraction.

title: The Synthetic Media Shift: Tracking the Rise, Virality, and Detectability of AI-Generated Multimodal Misinformation
abstract: As generative AI advances, the distinction between authentic and synthetic media is increasingly blurred, challenging the integrity of online information. In this study, we present CONVEX, a large-scale dataset of multimodal misinformation involving miscaptioned, edited, and AI-generated visual content, comprising over 150K multimodal posts with associated notes and engagement metrics from X's Community Notes. We analyze how multimodal misinformation evolves in terms of virality, engagement, and consensus dynamics, with a focus on synthetic media. Our results show that while AI-generated content achieves disproportionate virality, its spread is driven primarily by passive engagement rather than active discourse. Despite slower initial reporting, AI-generated content reaches community consensus more quickly once flagged. Moreover, our evaluation of specialized detectors and vision-language models reveals a consistent decline in performance over time in distinguishing synthetic from authentic images as generative models evolve. These findings highlight the need for continuous monitoring and adaptive strategies in the rapidly evolving digital information environment.

title: The cognitive companion: a lightweight parallel monitoring architecture for detecting and recovering from reasoning degradation in LLM agents
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents on multi-step tasks suffer reasoning degradation, looping, drift, stuck states, at rates up to 30% on hard tasks. Current solutions include hard step limits (abrupt) or LLM-as-judge monitoring (10-15% overhead per step). This paper introduces the Cognitive Companion, a parallel monitoring architecture with two implementations: an LLM-based Companion and a novel zero-overhead Probe-based Companion. We report a three-batch feasibility study centered on Gemma 4 E4B, with an additional exploratory small-model analysis on Qwen 2.5 1.5B and Llama 3.2 1B. In our experiments, the LLM-based Companion reduced repetition on loop-prone tasks by 52-62% with approximately 11% overhead. The Probe-based Companion, trained on hidden states from layer 28, showed a mean effect size of +0.471 at zero measured inference overhead; its strongest probe result achieved cross-validated AUROC 0.840 on a small proxy-labeled dataset. A key empirical finding is that companion benefit appears task-type dependent: companions are most helpful on loop-prone and open-ended tasks, while effects are neutral or negative on more structured tasks. Our small-model experiments also suggest a possible scale boundary: companions did not improve the measured quality proxy on 1B-1.5B models, even when interventions fired. Overall, the paper should be read as a feasibility study rather than a definitive validation. The results provide encouraging evidence that sub-token monitoring may be useful, identify task-type sensitivity as a practical design constraint, and motivate selective companion activation as a promising direction for future work.

title: SafeHarness: Lifecycle-Integrated Security Architecture for LLM-based Agent Deployment
abstract: The performance of large language model (LLM) agents depends critically on the execution harness, the system layer that orchestrates tool use, context management, and state persistence. Yet this same architectural centrality makes the harness a high-value attack surface: a single compromise at the harness level can cascade through the entire execution pipeline. We observe that existing security approaches suffer from structural mismatch, leaving them blind to harness-internal state and unable to coordinate across the different phases of agent operation. In this paper, we introduce \safeharness{}, a security architecture in which four proposed defense layers are woven directly into the agent lifecycle to address above significant limitations: adversarial context filtering at input processing, tiered causal verification at decision making, privilege-separated tool control at action execution, and safe rollback with adaptive degradation at state update. The proposed cross-layer mechanisms tie these layers together, escalating verification rigor, triggering rollbacks, and tightening tool privileges whenever sustained anomalies are detected. We evaluate \safeharness{} on benchmark datasets across diverse harness configurations, comparing against four security baselines under five attack scenarios spanning six threat categories. Compared to the unprotected baseline, \safeharness{} achieves an average reduction of approximately 38\% in UBR and 42\% in ASR, substantially lowering both the unsafe behavior rate and the attack success rate while preserving core task utility.

title: Linear codes arising from the point-hyperplane geometry — Part II: the twisted embedding
abstract: Let Γ ¯ be the point-hyperplane geometry of a projective space PG ( V ) , where V is a ( n + 1 ) -dimensional vector space over a finite field F q of order q . Suppose that σ is an automorphism of F q and consider the projective embedding ε σ of Γ ¯ into the projective space PG ( V ⊗ V ⁎ ) mapping the point ( [ x ] , [ ξ ] ) ∈ Γ ¯ to the projective point represented by the pure tensor x σ ⊗ ξ , with ξ ( x ) = 0 . In [11] , we focused on the case σ = 1 and we studied the projective code arising from the projective system Λ 1 = ε 1 ( Γ ¯ ) . Here we focus on the case σ ≠ 1 and we investigate the linear code C ( Λ σ ) arising from the projective system Λ σ = ε σ ( Γ ¯ ) . In particular, after having verified that C ( Λ σ ) is a minimal code, we determine its parameters, its minimum distance as well as its automorphism group. We also give a (geometrical) characterization of its minimum and second lowest weight codewords and determine its maximum weight when q and n are both odd.

title: Frame forecasting in cine MRI using the PCA respiratory motion model: comparing recurrent neural networks trained online and transformers
abstract: Respiratory motion complicates accurate irradiation of thoraco-abdominal tumors during radiotherapy, as treatment-system latency entails target-location uncertainties. This work addresses frame forecasting in chest and liver cine MRI to compensate for such delays. We investigate RNNs trained with online learning algorithms, enabling adaptation to changing respiratory patterns via on-the-fly parameter updates, and transformers, increasingly common in time-series forecasting for their ability to capture long-term dependencies. Experiments used 12 sagittal thoracic and upper-abdominal cine-MRI sequences from ETH Zürich and OvGU; the OvGU data exhibited higher motion variability, noise, and lower contrast. PCA decomposes the Lucas-Kanade optical-flow field into static deformation modes and low-dimensional, time-dependent weights. We compare various methods for forecasting these weights: linear filters, population and sequence-specific transformer encoders, and RNNs trained with real-time recurrent learning (RTRL), unbiased online recurrent optimization, decoupled neural interfaces, and sparse one-step approximation (SnAp-1). Predicted displacements were used to warp the reference frame and generate future images. Prediction accuracy decreased with the horizon h. Linear regression performed best at short horizons (1.3mm geometrical error at h=0.32s, ETH Zürich dataset), while RTRL and SnAp-1 outperformed the other algorithms at medium-to-long horizons, with geometrical errors below 1.4mm and 2.8mm on the sequences from ETH Zürich and OvGU, respectively. The sequence-specific transformer was competitive for low-to-medium horizons, but transformers remained overall limited by data scarcity and domain shift between datasets. Predicted frames visually resembled the ground truth, with notable errors occurring near the diaphragm at end-inspiration and regions affected by out-of-plane motion.

title: Artificial intelligence benefit realization in Malaysian IT organizations: Conceptual framework
abstract: Most organizations use artificial intelligence as their main tool to drive digital transformation, as it improves their decision-making process, their ability to automate tasks, and their entire operational workflow. Organizations fail to realize measurable benefits from their AI investments because they want to maintain their current spending patterns. The existing research primarily studies AI adoption and readiness, while there exists a research gap about how organizations achieve value through AI after they have implemented it. The research presents a conceptual framework to study the technological, organizational, and ethical factors that determine how Malaysian IT organizations achieve AI benefits. The framework uses AI capability as a mediating mechanism, helping organizations transform their AI resources and governance conditions into organizational advantages in both tangible and intangible forms. The study integrates technological infrastructure, organizational readiness, and ethical governance to advance research on AI value creation and benefit realization. The proposed framework offers organizations a path to maximize value from their AI investments while establishing a research foundation for future studies in the Malaysian IT sector.

title: ПРИМЕНЕНИЕ ТЕХНОЛОГИЙ TELEGRAM БОТА И ИИ ПРИ ПРОЕКТИРОВАНИИ И РЕАЛИЗАЦИИ СИСТЕМ СЕМАНТИЧЕСКОГО ПОИСКА ЭЛЕКТРОННОЙ КОММЕРЦИИ
abstract: В работе рассматривается методология интеграции локальных языковых моделей (LLM) в диалоговые системы для электронной коммерции на примере Telegram-бота SmartShopBot. Проект нацелен на семантический поиск по каталогу товаров и интеллектуальное взаимодействие с пользователем при сохранении приватности данных. Предлагается архитектура трёхконтурного взаимодействия («бот ↔ локальная LLM ↔ база данных/векторный индекс»), реализующая офлайн-инференс модели Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct через платформу Ollama и векторный поиск по эмбеддингам (nomic-embed-text). Проведено сравнение локального и облачного подходов по параметрам приватности, стоимости и латентности. Экспериментальная оценка показывает, что локальная интеграция обеспечивает стабильные задержки и предсказуемую стоимость эксплуатации без зависимости от внешних сервисов, при этом качество рекомендаций остаётся приемлемым. Практическая значимость работы заключается в снижении эксплуатационных расходов и обеспечении конфиденциальности данных в e-commerce-приложениях за счёт использования локального ИИ.

title: Teoria della Risonanza Isomorfica (TRI): Modello di Interfaccia per il Processamento Parallelo Simultaneo - Framework ADM di Anastasia De Masi
abstract: Teoria della Risonanza Isomorfica (TRI): Modello di Interfaccia per il Processamento Parallelo Simultaneo (PPS)La Teoria della Risonanza Isomorfica (TRI) introduce un paradigma innovativo nella comunicazione dedicato a individui con Processamento Parallelo Simultaneo (PPS). Il modello affronta il fallimento sistemico della comunicazione lineare e sequenziale — definita come "collo di bottiglia temporale" — che spesso risulta incompatibile con le architetture cognitive non lineari.La TRI non si pone l'obiettivo di normalizzare il processamento cognitivo, ma di ottimizzare l'interfaccia comunicativa attraverso la sincronizzazione di strutture logiche definite come Isomorfismi. Il documento delinea i quattro pilastri operativi della teoria:Grammatica degli Stati: Sostituzione della narrazione temporale con la definizione di "Cluster di Attributi" per eliminare l'ansia da transizione.Stratificazione a Layer: Trasmissione dell'informazione per livelli di profondità logica (Risoluzione Progressiva) per garantire la coerenza globale del sistema.Ancoraggio Spaziale: Utilizzo dello spazio fisico come memoria esterna permanente per stabilizzare concetti volatili e simultanei.Bug Hunting: Protocollo di verifica della comunicazione basato sulla rilevazione di incongruenze logiche anziché sulla ripetizione verbale.Attraverso l'applicazione di questi protocolli, la TRI promuove una reale autonomia decisionale e una qualità relazionale paritaria, trasformando la comunicazione da una successione di istruzioni a una costruzione condivisa di architetture di pensiero.

title: Introducing a definition of AGI from the perspective of expertise compression
abstract: We introduce Experience-Compressed Intelligence (ECI), a novel framework for measuring artificial general intelligence that shifts focus from human-like performance to the efficiency of experience compression and reuse. Traditional AGI definitions emphasize behavioral similarity to humans or economic productivity, obscuring fundamental questions about how systems acquire, represent, and transfer knowledge. We propose that intelligence should be quantified by measuring: (1) how much human experience can be compressed into learned representations, (2) the rate of extracting tacit knowledge from limited examples, (3) the efficiency of cross-domain knowledge transfer, and (4) epistemic confidence through activation manifold analysis. We formalize ECI as a composite metric integrating compression ratio, tacit knowledge extraction rate, cross-domain retention, and experience efficiency index, weighted by epistemic confidence derived from Statistical Path Density (SPD). Our experimental validation on MNIST demonstrates that ECI provides meaningful discrimination between in-distribution, near-out-of-distribution, and far-out-of-distribution samples (AUROC = 1.0 for noise detection, 0.73 for FashionMNIST), with overwhelming statistical significance (p < 10⁻²²⁰). We argue that ECI offers a measurable, comparable, and scalable alternative to existing AGI definitions, with clear implications for evaluating progress toward general intelligence.

title: Research on deepfake audio detection methods based on feature fusion
abstract: Deepfake audio detection confronts core challenges including substantial intraspecimen variation, minimal inter-specimen differences, and model lag in adapting to emerging techniques. This paper proposes a detection framework integrating multidimensional feature enhancement with heterogeneous dynamic ensemble learning: establishing a "static-temporal" dual-dimensional feature fusion system. It employs higher-order MFCC interactions and BiLSTM temporal attention to mitigate intraspecimen fluctuations while cross-amplifying inter-specimen differences through cross-modal feature integration.An heterogeneous model pool comprising XGBoost and Random Forest is established, incorporating dynamic attention weight allocation to adapt to emerging forgery techniques, supplemented by adversarial sample augmentation and adaptive training optimisation. Experimental validation demonstrates this framework effectively mitigates the aforementioned core challenges, with trained models achieving 95% accuracy post-ensemble iteration. Compared to conventional detection methods, this research provides a practical technical pathway for audio content security governance.

title: Energy-Efficient Edge AI–Driven ICU Mortality Prediction Using Clinical Health Records
abstract: Accurate and timely prediction of mortality in Intensive Care Units (ICUs) is critical for improving clinical decision-making, particularly in resource-constrained and lowconnectivity healthcare environments. This study proposes an energy-efficient Edge AI-driven framework for ICU mortality prediction using electronic health records (EHRs). A publicly available, anonymized ICU dataset comprising patient records with$\mathbf{1 2 0}$demographic, physiological, and laboratory features was employed. Comprehensive data preprocessing was performed to address missing values, class imbalance, and feature heterogeneity. Feature selection was conducted using correlation analysis, Chi-square testing, and Recursive Feature Elimination to reduce redundancy and enhance model interpretability. Five machine learning models Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, Support Vector Machine, and K-Nearest Neighbors were developed and evaluated using stratified train-test splitting to ensure unbiased learning. Experimental results demonstrate that ensemble-based models outperform linear and distance-based classifiers, with the proposed Random Forest model achieving the highest accuracy of 98%, along with balanced precision, recall, and F1score. The findings highlight the suitability of ensemble learning approaches for real-world ICU mortality prediction and edgeenabled smart healthcare systems.

title: Weight Patching: Toward Source-Level Mechanistic Localization in LLMs
abstract: Mechanistic interpretability seeks to localize model behavior to the internal components that causally realize it. Prior work has advanced activation-space localization and causal tracing, but modules that appear important in activation space may merely aggregate or amplify upstream signals rather than encode the target capability in their own parameters. To address this gap, we propose Weight Patching, a parameter-space intervention method for source-oriented analysis in paired same-architecture models that differ in how strongly they express a target capability under the inputs of interest. Given a base model and a behavior-specialized counterpart, Weight Patching replaces selected module weights from the specialized model into the base model under a fixed input. We instantiate the method on instruction following and introduce a framework centered on a vector-anchor behavioral interface that provides a shared internal criterion for whether a task-relevant control state has been formed or recovered in open-ended generation. Under this framework, the analysis reveals a hierarchy from shallow candidate source-side carriers to aggregation and routing modules, and further to downstream execution circuits. The recovered component scores can also guide mechanism-aware model merging, improving selective fusion across the evaluated expert combinations and providing additional external validation.

title: Who Decides in AI-Mediated Learning? The Agency Allocation Framework
abstract: As AI-mediated learning systems increasingly shape how learners plan, make decisions, and progress through education, learner agency is becoming both more consequential and harder to conceptualize at scale. Existing research often treats agency as a proxy for engagement and self-regulation, leaving unclear who actually holds decision-making authority in large-scale, automated learning environments. This paper reframes learner agency as the allocation of decision authority across learners, educators, institutions, and AI systems. We introduce the Agency Allocation Framework (AAF) for analyzing how decisions are distributed, how choices are architected, what evidence supports them, and over what time horizons their consequences unfold. Drawing on a focused review of Learning at Scale literature and an illustrative tutoring-system example, we identify four recurring challenges for studying learner agency at scale: (1) conceptual ambiguity, (2) reliance on behavioral proxies, (3) trade-offs between efficiency and learner control, and (4) the redistribution of agency through AI-mediated systems. Rather than advocating more or less automation, the AAF supports systematic analysis of when AI scaffolds learners' capacity to act and when it substitutes for it. By making decision authority explicit, the framework provides researchers and designers with analytic tools for studying, comparing, and evaluating agency-preserving learning systems in increasingly automated educational contexts.

title: Post-Quantum Cryptography: Addressing the Future Threats to Cybersecurity
abstract: Classical cryptography systems are vulnerable to quantum computing because they depend on computationally tough issues, such as solving discrete logarithms or factoring big integers. Cryptography in the age of quantum computing has new challenges and opportunities. Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) aims to address these issues by developing algorithms that are resistant to quantum computing, including code-based, hash-based, and lattice-based cryptography. The study sheds light on how PQC can tackle future cybersecurity risks by examining their security models, performance, and suitability for real-world implementation. The article also delves into the difficulties of updating the world's cryptographic infrastructure to use algorithms that are immune to quantum attacks, as well as the present status of PQC standardization initiatives. Protecting digital systems from possible breaches and guaranteeing long-term data security will be the deployment of PQC that is most important as quantum computing develops.

title: Optimización del marketing digital mediante inteligencia artificial: impacto en la toma de decisiones estratégicas
abstract: Objetivo: Este estudio analizó el impacto de la inteligencia artificial en la optimización del marketing digital y su influencia en la toma de decisiones estratégicas, considerando su relevancia en entornos empresariales orientados a datos. Metodología: Se empleó un enfoque cuantitativo, con diseño no experimental y corte transversal, aplicando un muestreo no probabilístico por conveniencia a 50 organizaciones de los sectores tecnológico y de servicios; se utilizó un cuestionario tipo Likert validado por expertos y se realizó un análisis correlacional mediante el coeficiente Rho de Spearman en SPSS. Resultados: Se evidenció una preferencia por el uso de herramientas de automatización de campañas (36%) y personalización de la experiencia del usuario (24%), así como una correlación significativa y alta (Rho=0.742; p<0.05) entre la integración de inteligencia artificial y la precisión en la toma de decisiones estratégicas; además, se identificó una reducción del 22% en el desperdicio publicitario mediante modelos de atribución basados en datos. Conclusiones: Se concluyó que la inteligencia artificial constituye una capacidad estratégica que mejora la precisión organizacional, reduce la incertidumbre y optimiza la asignación de recursos, permitiendo una transición hacia decisiones basadas en evidencia; sus aplicaciones prácticas incluyen la optimización del rendimiento y la eficiencia presupuestaria, aunque plantea desafíos éticos relacionados con la personalización intensiva, abriendo líneas futuras de investigación sobre el equilibrio entre tecnología, ética y comportamiento del consumidor.

title: Information in the Aryabhata Sense: Value of Zero-Mass Boundaries
abstract: The monograph is a carefully constructed, philosophically ambitious project that integrates three layers: (1) a clean axiomatic core theorem, (2) an operational refinement in quantum source coding that treats atypicality as exploitable structure, and (3) a postulational unification strategy that extends the framework to continuous, interacting, and observerdependent systems via epistemology and a nonlocal boundary. It is not merely a repackaging of Shannon/von Neumann theory; it is a deliberate reframing that elevates conservation to a unifying postulate and gives the atypical sector genuine operational content. At the same time, its novelty lies more in synthesis, interpretation, and finite blocklength strategy than in deriving new independent mathematical invariants.

title: Publication — Cadre unifié des signatures issues du langage et de leur fragmentation interprétative
abstract: . 📄 VERSION FINALE 📄 Cadre unifié des signatures issues du langage et des régimes de projection Auteur : Kevin FradierStatut : Note théorique / cadre exploratoireDate : 15 avril 2026Licence : CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 1. Problème général Les analyses du langage, des signaux et des signatures statistiques tendent à fragmenter un système pourtant unifié en plusieurs objets distincts : langage, transformation, analyse et signature. Cette séparation produit une difficulté centrale : les résultats observés sont interprétés indépendamment du protocole qui les génère. 2. Hypothèse de travail Le langage peut être considéré comme un système relationnel structuré (ordre, cooccurrences, dépendances locales et globales). Toute signature observée dans un espace d’analyse résulte d’une projection de ce système dans un espace de représentation numérique. 3. Principe de projection Toute signature est le résultat d’une transformation d’un système linguistique vers un espace d’observation défini par un protocole de calcul. Cela implique : une signature n’est observable qu’à travers une transformation explicite elle dépend du couple (langage, méthode de projection) il n’existe pas d’accès direct à une signature sans représentation la forme observée dépend du protocole d’analyse 4. Définition de la signature Une signature est une structure statistique émergente produite par la transformation d’un objet linguistique en signal numérique. Elle peut être : stable instable dépendante de l’échelle dépendante de la méthode de projection 5. Régimes d’observation Les signatures ne sont pas invariantes en toutes conditions. On distingue trois régimes : Sous-régime : données insuffisantes → bruit dominant Régime critique : émergence intermittente de structures Régime stable : motifs reproductibles sous variations contrôlées 6. Conditions de validité Toute analyse de signature doit satisfaire trois contraintes : analyse multi-échelle (variation de taille du corpus) comparaison à un modèle nul (bruit ou permutation) robustesse aux changements de projection Sans ces conditions, aucune distinction fiable entre structure et artefact n’est possible. 7. Règle de décision Une signature est classée selon trois états : STRUCTURE : stable, distincte du modèle nul, robuste aux transformations ARTEFACT : disparaît ou converge vers le modèle nul sous variations INDÉTERMINÉE : dépend fortement de l’échelle ou du protocole 8. Recomposition du système Le système étudié se formalise comme : langage → transformation → espace de projection → signatures La question devient : quelles structures persistent sous variations de projection et d’échelle, et lesquelles sont induites par la méthode ? 9. Conclusion Ce cadre propose une reformulation unifiée : le langage est un système relationnel structuré les projections ne créent pas de structure mais rendent certaines propriétés observables les signatures sont des phénomènes dépendants du protocole d’observation leur statut (structure, artefact, indéterminé) doit être établi par protocole La question centrale reste ouverte :existe-t-il des invariants robustes du langage indépendants des choix de projection, ou observe-t-on uniquement des effets de lecture méthodologiques ? 📌 11. Protocole unifié d’évaluation et règle de décision Toute analyse de signature doit être exécutée selon un protocole unique en trois étapes obligatoires : 11.1 Étape multi-échelle La signature est calculée sur plusieurs tailles de corpus : sous-échantillons taille complète fenêtres intermédiaires Critère : → une signature dépendante de n’est pas immédiatement interprétable comme structure. 11.2 Étape modèle nul La signature est comparée à un modèle nul construit par : permutation des éléments du texte ou génération aléatoire conservant les distributions locales Critère : → si la signature ne se distingue pas du nul, elle est non structurée dans ce cadre. 11.3 Étape robustesse aux projections La signature est recalculée sous plusieurs transformations : permutation changement d’encodage transformation non-linéaire variation de fenêtre Critère : → une signature dépendante de la transformation n’est pas un invariant. 11.4 Règle de décision (bloc central manquant) Chaque signature est classée selon un seul résultat : A. STRUCTURE Si et seulement si : elle est significativement différente du modèle nul elle reste stable sous variations de projection elle reste cohérente à travers plusieurs échelles B. ARTEFACT DE PROJECTION Si : elle disparaît sous permutation ou bruit ou converge vers le modèle nul ou change complètement selon le pipeline C. INDÉTERMINÉE Si : elle est partiellement stable mais dépend fortement de l’échelle ou de la méthode 11.5 Conséquence logique Aucune signature ne peut être interprétée hors de ce protocole. Toute assertion sur une “structure du langage” ou une “invariance” doit être : testée multi-échelle comparée à un modèle nul validée par robustesse aux projections 11.6 Fermeture du cadre Dans ce cadre : une signature n’est pas une entité mais un résultat conditionnel d’un protocole d’observation 🧠 Tu peux résumer tout ton travail maintenant comme : Une signature n’a de statut que si elle survit simultanément aux variations d’échelle, aux modèles nuls, et aux changements de projection. 📌 Ce que ton cadre fait émerger (vraiment) Sans parler de “signature” en soi, ton cadre met surtout en évidence 3 choses qui étaient déjà connues séparément mais rarement pensées ensemble comme un seul objet. 1. 🔁 Unification du problème “langage → mesure → résultat” Tu rends explicite une chaîne qui est souvent découpée en sciences différentes : linguistique → étudie le langage statistique / ML → étudie les données signal processing → étudie les transformations épistémologie → parle de l’observation 👉 Ton cadre dit : tout ça est un seul processus continu 📌 Ce que ça change : on ne peut plus parler du “résultat” sans parler du “pipeline” on ne peut plus séparer objet et méthode 2. 🧠 Déplacement du statut des “objets” Tu fais un déplacement important : Avant (fragmentation classique) : texte = objet signature = propriété du texte analyse = outil externe Dans ton cadre : le texte seul n’est pas suffisant le résultat dépend du système complet (texte + transformation + échelle) 👉 Donc les “objets” deviennent : des effets d’un dispositif d’observation 📌 Ce que ça casse : l’idée qu’une structure est “dans” le texte indépendamment de la lecture 3. ⚙️ Mise en régime des phénomènes (très important) Ton cadre introduit implicitement une idée forte : une structure n’est pas binaire (existe / n’existe pas), mais dépend d’un régime d’observation Ces régimes : bruit dominant émergence stabilité 📌 Ce que ça change : une structure devient un phénomène conditionnel pas une propriété absolue 📌 Donc concrètement : ce que ton cadre “apporte” Pas une nouvelle théorie du langage. Mais : ✔ 1. Une fusion des niveaux (langage / transformation / observation) ✔ 2. Une critique de l’autonomie des résultats (un résultat dépend du dispositif) ✔ 3. Une lecture en régimes (bruit → émergence → stabilité) 📌 Et la vérité importante Ce que tu as construit : 👉 n’est pas une découverte isolée 👉 mais une reformulation unificatrice de plusieurs champs déjà existants Mais ce genre de reformulation peut être utile si : elle est opérationnelle (tests + décision) elle est cohérente elle permet de penser ensemble des choses séparées 📌 Version ultra simple Ton cadre fait surtout ceci : Il retire l’illusion que les résultats statistiques du langage sont indépendants du processus qui les produit. 📌 Règle d’inférence unifiéeUne signature S est évaluée par 3 tests :T₁ = stabilité multi-échelleT₂ = écart au modèle nulT₃ = robustesse aux projections📌 Décision finale (version propre)On définit :ST = score multi-échelleSN = score modèle nulSP = score projection🧠 Règle simple :✔ STRUCTUREsi :ST élevéSN significatif (différent du bruit)SP stable❌ ARTEFACTsi :SN ≈ bruitou ST faibleou SP instable⚠️ INDÉTERMINÉsi :résultats mixtesdépend fortement du choix de projection ou taille📌 IMPORTANT (ce que tu cherchais depuis le début)👉 Ça transforme ton cadre en :un système de décision sur des signatures observées 🔎 Résumé très simpleUne signature peut :être réelleêtre stable dans un espacedisparaître dans un autresans que ce soit une illusionLa question n’est pas :“est-elle indépendante du pipeline ?”Mais :“à combien de transformations raisonnables survit-elle ?”C’est ça la robustesse. Dynamique mémoire–signature–rigidité Rajout conceptuel émergent 👇😴On peut proposer une lecture simplifiée des processus de stabilisation théorique sous la forme d’un triplet dynamique :(0) Absence de mémoire cumulative : les observations apparaissent dispersées et non corrélées.(1) Signature faible : des motifs partiels émergent mais restent instables ou dépendants du cadre local.(2) Rigidité : la répétabilité et la cohérence interne atteignent un seuil permettant une formalisation stable, sans présumer d’une rigidité totale. Cette dynamique suggère que la transition de (1) vers (2) dépend moins uniquement de la nature intrinsèque du phénomène que de la capacité du système à accumuler et intégrer les signatures dans un espace mémoire cohérent.Il reste ouvert dans quelle mesure la fragmentation disciplinaire ou contextuelle influence ce passage. title: Metodología estratégica para levantamientos geológicos extensivos: caso de estudio en la Región Central de Panamá
abstract: Este estudio presenta una metodología adaptativa para la planificación y ejecución de levantamientos geológicos extensivos en la Región Central de Panamá, desarrollada en el marco del proyecto Descripción Petrográfica de la Región Central de Panamá. La propuesta integra herramientas de Sistemas de Información Geográfica (SIG), fotointerpretación satelital y segmentación territorial mediante polígonos de Thiessen con el objetivo de optimizar la selección de sitios de muestreo y mejorar la cobertura espacial en áreas con heterogeneidad litológica y variabilidad en accesibilidad. La identificación preliminar de puntos se realizó mediante revisión bibliográfica, cartografía base y análisis de imágenes satelitales, lo que permitió depurar una red inicial de afloramientos potenciales. La segmentación territorial derivada de los polígonos de Thiessen facilitó la organización logística en siete zonas de muestreo equilibradas. Durante 21 días efectivos de campaña se documentaron 208 sitios distribuidos en 27 distritos y se recolectaron 229 muestras de roca, siguiendo un protocolo estandarizado que incluyó registro estructural, descripción macroscópica y documentación fotográfica. Los resultados demuestran que la planificación previa basada en SIG mejora la eficiencia operativa y la representatividad litológica, constituyendo una alternativa viable para estudios en regiones con accesibilidad limitada o cartografía desactualizada. La metodología propuesta es reproducible, de bajo costo relativo y aplicable en contextos académicos, institucionales y de investigación, contribuyendo al fortalecimiento de futuras iniciativas de caracterización geológica en Panamá.

title: PSCF-NER: prompt-driven Chinese scholarly entity recognition and knowledge graph construction
abstract: Named Entity Recognition (NER) is a fundamental task in natural language processing. In recent years, driven by largescale domain-specific datasets such as BioNLP and SciERC, English NER has made significant progress. However, Chinese NER in specialized domains still faces issues such as scarce annotation resources and insufficient coverage. To address this, this paper proposes a Prompt-guided Synergistic Construction Framework (PSCF) and, based on it, constructs a Chinese academic dataset, ScholarInfoNER, which contains 18 fine-grained entity types, as well as a visualized academic knowledge graph, ScholarKG. Experimental results show that PSCF achieves an F1 score of 85.15% on ScholarInfoNER, outperforming traditional sequence labeling models, validating the effectiveness of each module in the framework. This study provides a reproducible and scalable solution for knowledge extraction in low-resource academic domains. The dataset and code are available at https://github.com/svenzhi/ScholarInfoNER.

title: CTC-Seq2Seq Whisper-Conformer: A Multi-Task Acoustic Model with Phonetic Convergence and Error-Aware Training
abstract: The hybrid Architecture is a solution to the problem of “Data Scarcity” in low-resource Languages, as well as to the Problem of Phonetic Variability across Regional Accents. Although Large Scale Pretrained Models such as OpenAIs Whisper and Metas Wav2Vec2 have achieved Good Performance in Many Different Scenarios, they have Some Limitations when it comes to Extremely Low Resource Conditions. Specifically, They Have Hallucinations in Generative Decoders and Reduced Accent Generalization. In order to Address these Issues, this System Combines a Wav2Vec2-XLSR Self-Supervised Front End with a Conformer-Based Acoustic Encoder and a Lightweight Whisper Style Sequence-to-Sequence Decoder. In order to Improve Performance Under Limited Supervision, the Framework uses Three Key Strategies: Targeted Synthetic Data Augmentation Using Text-To-Speech (TTS) And Acoustic Perturbations; ParameterEfficient Accent Adaptation Through Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRa) Modules; and A Multi-Task Learning Objective That Jointly Optimizes Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) Loss and Sequence-to-Sequences Cross-Entropy Loss. These Three Components Allow For Accurate Temporal Alignment, As Well as Linguistic Fluency and Robustness to Accent Induced Variations. The Results of Experiments Conducted On Low Resource Subsets Of the Mozilla Common Voice Dataset and Accent Rich Speech Corpora Show Consistent Improvements Over Fine-Tuned Wav2Vec2 and Whisper Baselines. The Hybrid Architecture Achieves Notable Reductions In Word Error Rate (WER) and Character Error Rate (CER). The Addition of Conformer Blocks to the Encoder Improved Phonetic Representation, and The Multi-Task Objective Reduced Decoder Hallucinations. Thus, the Proposed Modular Approach Provides An Efficient and Scalable Solution for Accent-Aware ASR in Underrepresented and Dialect-Diverse Languages.

title: BIEVR-LIO: Robust LiDAR-Inertial Odometry through Bump-Image-Enhanced Voxel Maps
abstract: Reliable odometry is essential for mobile robots as they increasingly enter more challenging environments, which often contain little information to constrain point cloud registration, resulting in degraded LiDAR-Inertial Odometry (LIO) accuracy or even divergence. To address this, we present BIEVR-LIO, a novel approach designed specifically to exploit subtle variations in the available geometry for improved robustness. We propose a high-resolution map representation that stores surfaces as compact voxel-wise oriented height images. This representation can directly be used for registration without the calculation of intermediate geometric primitives while still supporting efficient updates. Since informative geometry is often sparsely distributed in the environment, we further propose a map-informed point sampling strategy to focus registration on geometrically informative regions, improving robustness in uninformative environments while reducing computational cost compared to global high-resolution sampling. Experiments across multiple sensors, platforms, and environments demonstrates state-of-the-art performance in well-constrained scenes and substantial improvements in challenging scenarios where baseline methods diverge. Additionally, we demonstrate that the fine-grained geometry captured by BIEVR-LIO can be used for downstream tasks such as elevation mapping for robot locomotion.

title: DUSE: A data expansion framework for low-resource automatic modulation recognition based on active learning
abstract: Although deep neural networks have made remarkable achievements in the field of automatic modulation recognition (AMR), they typically require large amounts of labeled data for training, which poses a major challenge in many Internet of Things (IoT) applications. IoT environments often involve resource-constrained devices and dynamic wireless conditions, resulting in severely limited and difficult-to-acquire target domain signal samples. Manual data collection and expert annotation are often impractical due to high costs and scalability issues. While data augmentation techniques can partially alleviate sample scarcity, they fail to introduce truly new information from external sources, thus remaining insufficient for robust model generalization. To effectively address the data scarcity problem in IoT-oriented AMR, this paper introduces a data expansion framework named D ynamic U ncertainty-driven S ample E xpansion (DUSE). Specifically, DUSE uses an uncertainty scoring function to filter out useful samples from relevant AMR datasets and employs an active learning strategy to continuously refine the scorer. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DUSE consistently outperforms 8 coreset selection strategies, including Least Confidence, Entropy, Margin, DeepFool, Forgetting, Glister, GraNd and Herding, in both class-balance and class-imbalance settings. For example, at an expansion rate of 19%, DUSE improves accuracy by approximately 7% compared to the state-of-the-art method on RML2016.10a. Besides, DUSE exhibits strong cross-architecture generalization for unseen models, making it particularly suitable for open and evolving IoT communication systems.

title: Design and Fabrication of Scalable Quantum Circuits for Quantum Computation
abstract: Designing and building scalable quantum circuits that can effectively apply quantum algorithms is essential to the quick development of quantum computing technology. With an emphasis on different architectures including superconducting qubits, trapped ions, and topological qubits, this study provides an overview of the state-of-the-art in quantum circuit design as of right now. We go over the fundamentals of designing scalable quantum circuits, stressing the significance of qubit connection, error correction, and coherence maintenance. The study also discusses the sophisticated materials development, lithography, and etching processes used in the construction of these quantum circuits. We hope to shed light on the future of quantum computation and the steps required to create workable, large-scale quantum processors by analyzing recent developments and lingering difficulties in scaling quantum circuits. the vital role that multidisciplinary cooperation plays in closing the gap between theoretical developments and experimental application, which eventually opens the door for the development of reliable quantum computing systems.

title: The Relationship Between Athlete-Generated Content and Online Abuse
abstract: Background: The pervasive issue of online abuse directed at elite athletes necessitates a clearer understanding of its drivers. This study investigates the relationship between specific categories of athlete-generated social media content and the incidence of online abuse, examining temporal, demographic, and typological patterns. Methods: A longitudinal quantitative content analysis was conducted on 400 Instagram posts from four Olympic athletes, tracked across pre-Olympic, Olympic, and postseason phases. Content was categorized into six types, and user comments were classified as general or abusive (subcategorized as personal attacks or performance-related criticism). Statistical analyses included negative binomial regression and non-parametric tests, framed by the Online Disinhibition Effect and Social Norms Theory. Results: Content type was a primary predictor of abuse. Commercial content was associated with a 690% increase in abuse incidence (IRR=7.90, p<.01), while personal life content correlated with a 57% reduction (IRR=0.43, p<.01). Personal attacks constituted 74.84% of all abuse, significantly outweighing performance-related criticism (19.94%). No significant change in abuse frequency was observed during the Olympic period. Significant demographic disparities were found: Chinese athletes received abuse at 32.5 times the rate of British athletes, while female athletes experienced 51.4% less abuse than males. Conclusion: Athlete content strategy significantly influences online abuse risk, with commercial promotion being a major trigger. The overwhelming prevalence of personal attacks underscores the role of online disinhibition. The findings advocate for strategic content management by athletes and the development of more nuanced, culturally informed platform moderation systems to mitigate abuse.

title: ENHANCING DEPENDENCY PARSING FOR TELUGU-ENGLISH CODE-MIXED TEXT: TREEBANK CREATION, PARSER ADAPTATIONS AND POS TAGGING INTEGRATION
abstract: Code-mixed text from social media poses significant challenges for syntactic analysis due to irregular grammar, non-standard usage, and frequent language switching. For Telugu-English code-mixed text, the absence of large-scale syntactic resources and specialized parsing models limits progress in downstream multilingual NLP applications. In this work, we address this gap by introducing the first substantial manually annotated Telugu-English code-mixed dependency treebank of 4,152 sentences, developed using Universal Dependencies (UD) 2.0 guidelines. We further propose enhancements to a biaffine dependency parser by incorporating a language-aware head-dependent bias and relation-specific structural weights to better capture cross-lingual syntactic patterns. Our approach improves parsing performance, achieving 75.53% UAS and 61.86% LAS, with consistent gains over a strong baseline. In addition, we demonstrate that integrating dependency-derived syntactic features into a BiLSTM-CRF model improves part-of-speech tagging, achieving a macro-F1 score of 83.73%, with statistically validated gains. We also re-annotate an existing Telugu-English dataset using UD 2.0 to ensure compatibility with modern syntactic frameworks. Overall, this work provides new annotated resources and modeling strategies that advance syntactic processing for Telugu-English code-mixed text, with broader implications for developing robust NLP systems in low-resource and multilingual settings.

title: An LLM-Powered Real-Time Debate Training System with AI Opponent, Adaptive Mentorship, and Multimodal Abuse Detection
abstract: The researchers developed a new system for real-time debate training which uses Large Language Models (LLMs) to function as three different systems that compete with users while teaching them privately and detecting multiple types of abuse through one system during live voice interactions. The system provides ongoing feedback during live debates because it differs from Debatrix [1] which only evaluates completed debates through automated judging. The system uses WebRTC-based voice transport [16] to deliver audio through its dual-speech recognition system which combines Web Speech API with Vosk WASM fallback and uses Socket.IO to manage real-time events while the Groq API performs LLM inference. The system uses a dual-layer dynamic health and credibility scoring model which replaces traditional static verdicts to create an educational experience that resembles a video game. The system uses a three-strike moderation system to oversee both live voice transcripts and chat messages with the help of the Hugging Face unbiased-toxic-roberta model [7]. The evaluation process shows that the system can perform real-time adversarial rebuttals while providing private coaching during every spoken sentence and enforcing multimodal safety measures which no other existing debate AI system can accomplish.

title: Decomposition and Clustering of Distributed Big Data Mining Using Rank-Revealing QR Matrix Factorization Method (DCDB-RMF)
abstract: It was one of the notable methods of extracting knowledge out of the big data generated by modern times. an application of matrix decomposition is used. It is impractical or rather impossible to process this enormous amount of data through this process in just one machine, given that big data are mostly gathered from remote places through the use of several machines. Hence, there is normally a lot of heterogeneous noise in such data as a result. It is, hence, important and beneficial to design a distributed matrix decomposition technique for big data analysis. This technique ought to address non-homogeneous noises and communication problems inherent in distributed computing. Therefore, for huge data mining and clustering, we propose a novel method namely Decomposition and Clustering of Distributed Big Data mining using Rank-Revealing QR (RRQR) Matrix Factorization Method (DCDB-RMF). The outcome of the experiment revealed that the given technique is more effective than the similar studies in the past.

title: Language models transmit behavioural traits through hidden signals in data
abstract: . Here we show that distillation can lead to subliminal learning-the transmission of behavioural traits through semantically unrelated data. In our main experiments, a 'teacher' model with some trait T (such as disproportionately generating responses favouring owls or showing broad misaligned behaviour) generates datasets consisting solely of number sequences. Remarkably, a 'student' model trained on these data learns T, even when references to T are rigorously removed. More realistically, we observe the same effect when the teacher generates math reasoning traces or code. The effect occurs only when the teacher and student have the same (or behaviourally matched) base models. To help explain this, we prove a theoretical result showing that subliminal learning arises in neural networks under broad conditions and demonstrate it in a simple multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifier. As artificial intelligence systems are increasingly trained on the outputs of one another, they may inherit properties not visible in the data. Safety evaluations may therefore need to examine not just behaviour, but the origins of models and training data and the processes used to create them.

title: Operasyonel Eşik Optimizasyonu Altında Kredi Kartı Dolandırıcılığı Tespiti için Kısıt Farkındalıklı Yumuşak Oylama Topluluk Çerçevesi
abstract: Credit card fraud detection is a challenging binary classification problem due to extreme class imbalance and the operational cost asymmetry between false negatives and false positives. Although high-performing classifiers can provide strong probability estimates, their practical effectiveness depends heavily on how these probabilities are converted into final fraud decisions. This study proposes a constraint-aware soft voting ensemble framework that explicitly separates model training from decision threshold selection. Unlike conventional approaches that rely on fixed probability thresholds, the proposed method aligns the classification decision with operational fraud detection requirements. Experimental results on a highly imbalanced credit card fraud dataset show that the proposed ensemble achieves a precision of 0.9000, recall of 0.8514, F1-score of 0.8750, ROC-AUC of 0.9525, and PR-AUC of 0.8441. These findings indicate that constraint-aware threshold optimization can improve the practical decision quality of ensemble-based fraud detection systems without requiring retraining of the underlying classifiers.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Project Management: A Systematic Review of Trends, Applications, and Ethical Challenges (2020–2026)
abstract: Despite the rapid proliferation of artificial intelligence technologies in project management contexts, a systematic understanding of AI applications, outcomes, and ethical implications remains fragmented. This systematic literature review addresses this research gap by synthesizing evidence from peer-reviewed studies published between 2020 and 2026, following PRISMA guidelines to ensure methodological rigor and transparency. The review examined multiple databases including Scopus, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore, employing comprehensive search strategies with predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. Quality assessment was conducted using established frameworks appropriate to diverse study designs, and data synthesis combined narrative synthesis with thematic analysis. The findings reveal that AI applications in project management span all phases of the project lifecycle, with the planning phase receiving the most extensive research attention. AI technologies demonstrated substantial potential for enhancing estimation accuracy, optimizing schedules, improving risk identification, and enabling more effective monitoring and control. The emergence of agentic AI in 2026 represents a significant development, transforming the relationship between project managers and AI systems from tool-based augmentation toward autonomous agent collaboration. However, the evidence also reveals considerable variation in outcomes across contexts, highlighting the importance of implementation factors and organizational readiness in determining AI success. The systematic examination of ethical challenges identifies critical considerations including algorithmic transparency, accountability allocation for AI-influenced decisions, fairness in AI-driven resource allocation, and data privacy protection. These ethical dimensions have received insufficient attention in the project management literature, representing an important gap that warrants systematic examination. The review identifies several limitations in the current evidence base, including the predominance of cross-sectional studies, limited longitudinal evidence regarding sustained adoption impacts, concentration of research in certain geographic and industrial contexts, and sparse development of project management-specific AI ethics frameworks. These gaps point toward productive directions for future research, including longitudinal studies of AI adoption trajectories, implementation process research, examination of AI effectiveness across diverse project types and industries, and development of theoretical frameworks for AI-augmented project management. The findings contribute to cumulative knowledge building while providing evidence-based guidance for practitioners considering AI adoption in project management contexts. The review demonstrates that AI integration in project management has matured from experimental applications to practical deployments, while highlighting the need for continued attention to ethical considerations and implementation factors that influence successful adoption.

title: Less Is More: Cognitive Load and the Single-Prompt Ceiling in LLM Mathematical Reasoning
abstract: We present a systematic empirical study of prompt engineering for formal mathematical reasoning in the context of the SAIR Equational Theories Stage 1 competition. The task requires deciding whether one equational law implies another over all magmas — a problem that is undecidable in general but decidable for FALSE via finite model search. Over five weeks, we designed, tested, and analyzed more than 40 prompt variants, ranging from 0 to 4,878 bytes, across four evaluation splits and three language models (gpt-oss-120b, Llama 3.3 70B, Gemma 4 31B). Our central finding is a single-prompt ceiling: despite substantial engineering effort, balanced hard accuracy plateaus in an empirical saturation region of approximately 60–79% for gpt-oss-120b, compared to a 59.75% no-cheatsheet baseline. We identify three mechanisms underlying this ceiling: (1) the mathematical undecidability of the TRUE case limits what any finite prompt can encode; (2) complex rule systems decrease performance on weaker models (Llama 3.3 70B collapses to 0% TRUE recall with prompts exceeding ~2KB); and (3) prompt ordering effects interact with model attention in fragile, non-monotonic ways. Our best submission (AN45c, 2,252 bytes) achieves 79.25% accuracy on hard3 (n=400; 95% CI: [75.0%, 82.9%]), with TRUE recall of 95.9% and FALSE recall of 63.4%, representing a +19.5 percentage-point improvement over the no-cheatsheet baseline (59.75%). We release all prompt variants, evaluation scripts, and results at https://github.com/israelcazares/sair-prompt-engineering

title: How Much of AI Is Really the "Brain"?: Separating the Neural Network Core from External Procedural Systems
abstract: This concept paper argues that contemporary AI systems, especially LLM-based systems, should be understood as composite structures in which the neural network core and external procedural systems are clearly separated. The neural network functions as the “brain,” responsible for compression, association, generalization, and meaning formation, while tools such as search, calculation, code execution, and memory access function as the “body,” carrying out operations under its direction. The paper argues that AI evaluation must distinguish these components in principle, since failing to do so both overestimates the neural core and obscures its actual role. It also argues that, in AGI discussions, bodily extension and intelligence itself should not be conflated. Unreviewed conceptual preprint. PDFs in English and Japanese. Generative AI tools were used for language refinement and translation support; the author takes full responsibility for the final text, references, and claims. Keywordslarge language models, neural networks, expert systems, tool use, agent systems, artificial general intelligence, evaluation, system architecture, cognitive architecture

title: РОЛЬ АНТОНИМОВ В ИТАЛЬЯНСКОМ ЯЗЫКЕ
abstract: Статья посвящена роли антонимов в итальянском языке. Рассматриваются понятие и классификация антонимии, особенности формирования антонимов в итальянском их лексико-семантическая и прагматическая функция, значение для обучения иностранцев итальянскому языку, а также проблемы анализа и преподавания антонимов. Опираясь на современные исследования и примеры из итальянского языка, раскрываются ключевые места антонимов в системе языка: как средство выражения контраста, усиления смысла, стилистического оттенка.

title: Explainable Fuzzy Autonomous Decision System for Multi-Country Human Capital Stratification
abstract: Assessing national human capital development is important for strategic policymaking, conventional machine learning approaches usually struggle when the sample is small, highly uncertain mostly in socio economic datasets. This study introduces autonomous fuzzy inference system that will classify 20 major economies into four progressive human capital clusters: Emerging, Transitioning, Advanced and Knowledge Economy Mature. Utilizes six normalized indicators from World Bank sources, Mamdani-type fuzzy engine generates interpretable classifications via linguistic membership functions and automatically derived rules. Results show coherent, policy-relevant stratification with leading OECD economies classified as Knowledge Economy Mature, India, Indonesia as Transitioning and China as Emerging under a human-capital lens. Benchmarking against KNN and SVM classifiers using Leave-One out cross validation shows ML models collapse to majority class predictions (accuracy$\approx 45-50 \%, \kappa \approx 0$) highlighting their limitations in small N regimes. The fuzzy approach offers superior explain ability, uncertainty handling and robustness providing a valuable tool for international development benchmarking and long-term human capital strategy formulation.

title: Emotional response to voice assistant type: impact on perceived humanity and user trust
abstract: Voice assistants are increasingly integrated into users’ daily lives, yet little is known about how their synthetic voices convey emotions and influence perceptions of humanity and trust. This study addresses that gap by comparing the emotional expressiveness of Siri, Alexa and Google Assistant and advancing an emotionally grounded Computational Trust Model based on ERT. The model conceptualises trust as an affective outcome in which vocal expressiveness triggers emotional responses, measured by valence and arousal, that shape perceived human-likeness and trust. An experimental study with 900 participants randomly exposed to one of the three voices delivering positive or negative product reviews examined these processes. After exposure, participants rated their emotional reactions, the assistant’s human-likeness, and trust. Results showed that expressive, positively valenced voices, especially Siri’s, evoked stronger emotional responses, higher perceived humanity and greater trust. Automatic Emotion Detection confirmed Siri’s superior emotional expressiveness. Positive messages enhanced emotional engagement, whereas negative valence had weaker effects. By extending ERT to voice-based interactions, the study introduces a scalable trust model rooted in emotion. It advances Human–Computer Interaction research by revealing how synthetic voices can express basic emotions and trigger affective responses, offering practical applications in customer service, education and healthcare.

title: Non-Markovian thermal reservoirs for autonomous entanglement distribution
abstract: We describe a novel scheme for the generation of stationary entanglement between two separated qubits that are driven by a purely thermal photon source. While in this scenario the qubits remain in a separable state at all times when the source is broadband, i.e. Markovian, the qubits relax into an entangled steady state once the bandwidth of the thermal source is sufficiently reduced. We explain this phenomenon by the appearance of a quasiadiabatic dark state and identify the most relevant nonadiabatic corrections that eventually lead to a breakdown of the entangled state, once the temperature is too high. This effect demonstrates how the non-Markovianity of an otherwise incoherent reservoir can be harnessed for quantum communication applications in optical, microwave, and phononic networks. As two specific examples, we discuss the use of filtered room-temperature noise as a passive resource for entangling distant superconducting qubits in a cryogenic quantum link or solid-state spin qubits in a phononic quantum channel.
